B. Is this measure already running in Kanta-Häme wellbeing services county (or in the Tays university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated. Every stage I patient who is too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy (3-8 visits, no anaesthesia) instead of being left without treatment. The treatment exists in every university hospital; what is missing in some counties is the referral rule.
effect_summary_en: In a Dutch national cancer registry study of elderly stage I patients, 7% fewer went untreated once stereotactic radiotherapy was fully available. The study does not measure the effect on the share of all lung cancer patients.
supported_en: A Netherlands Cancer Registry study (Annals of Oncology 2012) found 7% fewer untreated elderly stage I patients after stereotactic radiotherapy became available.
not_supported_en: The pages do not show the assumed 0.8-point rise in the curative share of all patients, or any figure for Finland or Kanta-Häme.
in_use_quote: Pieniin kasvaimiin voidaan antaa muutamalla hoitokerralla toteutettavaa täsmäsädehoitoa, johon yleensä liittyy hyvin vähän sivuvaikutuksia.
missing_en: No page shows a written rule that every stage I patient too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy, or an audit that checks this happens.
summary_en: Pirkanmaa wellbeing services county (pirha.fi), which runs Tays, has a lung cancer care-pathway page (dated 19.8.2026). It says a multidisciplinary team assesses whether each patient can get curative treatment, and that patients who cannot be operated can get precision radiotherapy (täsmäsädehoito) in a few sessions for small tumours. No page says that every frail stage I patient must be referred. On the effect, a Netherlands Cancer Registry study found 7% fewer elderly stage I patients left untreated once stereotactic radiotherapy was available, but it does not measure the effect on the share of all lung cancer patients.
unanswered_en: I looked for a written referral rule for frail stage I patients, Kanta-Häme's own pathway pages, and Finnish data on how many of these patients go untreated, and did not find them.
